APL synapses project · step-by-step reports · Report 03 · 2026-10-23

Odor-weighted maps of APL synapses

QuestionHow does each APL synapse in the calyx get an odor response, how are the odor-weighted maps drawn, and does weighting by APL's synapses on claws change how similar two odors look?
Inputs
  • Yang's ORN table ORN_ovlp16_resp_flyave_merge_dropna.csv (36 glomeruli × 16 odors, fly means)
  • Yang's per-fly ORN pickles orn_resp_megamat_trialmean_resp.pkl (9 flies, 17 odors) and orn_resp_validation2_trialmean_resp.pkl (5 flies, 22 odors)
  • Yang's GH146 PN imaging GH146_ij_certain-roi_stats.csv (7 flies, 29 glomeruli, 41 odor presentations, 3 repeats)
  • The APL tables, claws and boutons of Reports 01 and 02
Outputs
  • odor_weighted/PN_APL_synapses_*_weighted.csv, KC_APL_synapses_on_claws_by_glomerulus.csv (synapse tables with weights)
  • odor_weighted/*_map_*_posterior_view.png (the maps)
  • ORN_fly_means_by_glomerulus.csv, GH146_mean_by_glomerulus.csv
  • odor_weighted/odor_similarity_KC_APL_on_claws.csv/.png
Scripts
  • scripts/odor_meta.py, odor_maps.py, gh146_maps.py, glom_maps.py, orn_load.py, orn_maps.py, claw_glom_maps.py, gh146_per_odor_maps.py, odor_similarity.py
  • scripts/reports/r03_odor_maps.py (this report)

The maps were made to see where in the calyx APL meets the PNs and claws that a given odor drives. The same glomerulus-to-response step is what feeds odors into the model (Report 05), so it is described here in full. All maps are in both versions of the tables (official ROIs, and with the synapses outside them added; Report 02).

1Odor responses per glomerulus

Three response tables from Yang are used. The ORN table gives the response of the olfactory receptor neurons of each glomerulus (pebbled imaging) to the 16 odors of the TNT / TNT3c experiment; it is the input to the model. The per-fly ORN pickles give the same kind of response per fly, for 39 odors in two panels (megamat: 17 odors at 10⁻³; validation2: 22 odors at several dilutions). The GH146 table gives peak ΔF/F of the projection neurons (GH146 line) in 29 glomeruli, per fly and trial, for 41 odor presentations (24 in a "diagnostics" panel and 17 in megamat). Each is averaged over flies:

rˉg,o  =  1∣Fg,o∣∑f ∈ Fg,org,o(f)(1)\bar r_{g,o} \;=\; \frac{1}{|\mathcal{F}_{g,o}|} \sum_{f \,\in\, \mathcal{F}_{g,o}} r^{(f)}_{g,o} \tag{1}rˉg,o​=∣Fg,o​∣1​f∈Fg,o​∑​rg,o(f)​(1)
ORN: flies where the glomerulus was imaged (missing values skipped). GH146: every fly has 3 repeats, so the mean over flies and repeats equals the mean of per-fly means.

The fly means of the ORN pickles reproduce the ORN table exactly (largest difference 2 × 10⁻¹⁶), so the table is the same data. For the 16 model odors GH146 has 13: the 12 megamat odors at 10⁻³ and paa at 10⁻⁵ (diagnostics panel); −aPine, euc and B-myr were not presented.

2Giving each synapse a glomerulus

  • PN ↔ APL synapses. The PN's cell type names its glomerulus (e.g. DM1_lPN → DM1). Only uniglomerular types count. Types that name two glomeruli (VP1d+VP4, VP1m+VP5, VP3+VP1l) count for both; "X+" types (VP2+, VP3+) count for X. Multiglomerular (M_) and untyped PNs get no glomerulus: 1.2–1.4% of PN ↔ APL calyx synapses.
  • KC ↔ APL synapses. Only synapses on a claw (KC-side site within 2 µm of the claw, Report 02) get a glomerulus: that of the claw's main PN. 18–27% of KC → APL and 30–49% of APL → KC calyx synapses are on a claw (lowest in BANC; Report 02, Figure 3).
  • Names. Hemibrain uses older names for three glomeruli; they are renamed to FlyWire's (VC3l → VC3, VC3m → VC5, VC5 → VM6), which the response tables use.

Each synapse eee then carries, for each odor, the response of its glomerulus:

wo(e)  =  rˉg(e), o(2)w_o(e) \;=\; \bar r_{g(e),\,o} \tag{2}wo​(e)=rˉg(e),o​(2)
Blank (drawn gray) when g(e)g(e)g(e) is not in the response table, or eee has no glomerulus.

3Drawing the maps

Each panel shows one calyx in posterior view (Report 02, Table 2): every calyx synapse of the chosen kind is a dot at its position, colored by wo(e)w_o(e)wo​(e); synapses without a response are gray. The color scale follows Yang's GH146 heatmap PDF: the red–blue map RdBu_r with a two-slope normalization, so 0 is white, vmin⁡v_{\min}vmin​ is the darkest blue and vmax⁡v_{\max}vmax​ the darkest red:

c(v)  =  RdBu_r(t(v)),t(v)={12+12 v/vmax⁡v≥012−12 v/vmin⁡v<0(3)c(v) \;=\; \mathrm{RdBu\_r}\big(t(v)\big),\qquad t(v) = \begin{cases} \tfrac12 + \tfrac12\, v / v_{\max} & v \ge 0 \\ \tfrac12 - \tfrac12\, v / v_{\min} & v < 0 \end{cases} \tag{3}c(v)=RdBu_r(t(v)),t(v)={21​+21​v/vmax​21​−21​v/vmin​​v≥0v<0​(3)
t∈[0,1]t \in [0, 1]t∈[0,1] is the position along the color map. One scale is used for all odors of a map, set by the whole mean matrix.

The first maps (PA, PAA, MS with the ORN table) drew negative responses as 0; all later maps use the signed two-slope scale above. Within a panel, dots are drawn in order of increasing ∣wo∣|w_o|∣wo​∣, so strong responses sit on top.

The strongest boutons and claws of an odor are scattered over the whole calyx rather than gathered in one place: for PA, PAA and MS the response-weighted center of mass lies within 3 µm of the calyx center in FlyWire, hemibrain and male CNS. Some glomeruli do sit in typical places (DM1, the strongest PAA glomerulus, on the ventral rim; DL1, the strongest MS glomerulus, near the center).

Per-glomerulus maps

Two more map sets show, for each of 58 glomeruli in turn, that glomerulus's synapses in color and all others in gray: glomerulus_map_{PN_to_APL,APL_to_PN}_posterior_view.png (PN boutons) and claw_glomerulus_map_{KC_to_APL,APL_to_KC}_posterior_view.png (claws). They use no odor data.

4Odor-pair similarity of on-claw APL synapses

If APL's synapses on claws favored some glomeruli, two odors could look more or less alike "through APL's eyes" than through the glomeruli alone. To test this, each odor becomes a vector over all on-claw KC ↔ APL synapses of a dataset (both APLs), with entry wo(e)w_o(e)wo​(e); synapses whose glomerulus has no response are left out. The similarity of two odors is the Pearson correlation of their vectors. Because all synapses of a glomerulus carry the same value, this equals a correlation over glomeruli in which glomerulus ggg counts ngn_gng​ times, ngn_gng​ being its number of on-claw synapses:

ρab  =  ∑gng (rˉg,a−μa)(rˉg,b−μb)∑gng (rˉg,a−μa)2  ∑gng (rˉg,b−μb)2,μa=∑gngrˉg,a∑gng(4)\rho_{ab} \;=\; \frac{\sum_g n_g\,(\bar r_{g,a} - \mu_a)(\bar r_{g,b} - \mu_b)}{\sqrt{\sum_g n_g\,(\bar r_{g,a} - \mu_a)^2}\;\sqrt{\sum_g n_g\,(\bar r_{g,b} - \mu_b)^2}},\qquad \mu_a = \frac{\sum_g n_g \bar r_{g,a}}{\sum_g n_g} \tag{4}ρab​=∑g​ng​(rˉg,a​−μa​)2​∑g​ng​(rˉg,b​−μb​)2​∑g​ng​(rˉg,a​−μa​)(rˉg,b​−μb​)​,μa​=∑g​ng​∑g​ng​rˉg,a​​(4)
The "responses only" reference sets every ng=1n_g = 1ng​=1.

In every dataset, direction and response table the weighted similarities track the unweighted ones closely (r 0.945–0.986 over the 16 combinations), and the four connectomes agree with each other (r ≥ 0.947 between any two). So the glomerular distribution of APL's on-claw synapses does not by itself reshape odor similarity. Whether APL's activity reshapes the KC representation is a different question, taken up with a model from Report 05 on.

Pearson here, cosine later

This section uses the Pearson correlation (built 2026-10-14). From 2026-10-21 on, Yang asked for cosine similarity, as in their RDMs; the model and the TNT comparison (Reports 05–11) use cosine. odor_similarity.py was not switched.
